data.title: Is Coinbase Global (COIN) Undervalued After Wirex Put Tokenized Stocks On Base?
data.description:
Wirex’s launch of tokenized U.S. equities on Coinbase’s Base network places Coinbase Global (COIN) more deeply into the plumbing of onchain finance, linking its infrastructure to 24/7 stock exposure for millions of users.

For investors watching the ticker, Coinbase Global’s share price has come under pressure, with a 1 day share price return that declined 4.02%, a 30 day share price return that fell 33.58%, and a year to date share price return that dropped 51.37%. The 3 year total shareholder return remains positive at 9.03%, while the 1 year total shareholder return declined 56.06%. This points to fading short term momentum despite onchain moves like Wirex’s tokenized stocks launch and Coinbase’s recent work on tokenized rights, futures products, and post quantum custody.

Spot opportunities across onchain finance by scanning our hand picked 21 cryptocurrency and blockchain stocks, which, like Coinbase Global, sits at the intersection of tokenization, trading access, and blockchain infrastructure.

Coinbase Global is pushing deeper into tokenized finance while its own stock has been under clear pressure. The platform story looks strong. The price you pay for that exposure is the real question.

Most Popular Narrative: 54% Undervalued

Against a last close of $115.02, the most followed narrative on Coinbase Global pegs fair value at $247.39, framing the recent share price slide as a potential disconnect rather than a verdict on the business model.

The simplest way I can think about it is that Coinbase behaves a bit like a leveraged crypto proxy. If crypto prices rise materially over the next 5 to 10 years, Coinbase’s earnings power could expand much faster than the underlying asset because a lot of the operating base should be relatively stable.

See why 28 investors see Coinbase Global as 54% undervalued.

The view from QuanD, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, hinges on whether crypto becomes a much larger asset class over time, with Coinbase Global collecting more fees as volumes, custody balances, and subscription products scale on a relatively fixed cost base.

This storyline sits alongside the data. Coinbase Global reported revenue of $5.44b with an annual revenue growth rate of 15.70%, while still posting a net loss of $701.62m and a negative return on equity. Forecasts point to earnings growth of 63.16% per year and a path to profitability within three years, although the business is currently unprofitable and its future return on equity is expected to reach 13.5%, which screens as relatively low against higher quality benchmarks.

Analysts as a group have a price target around $195.00, which is 41.02% above the last close, but the data shows that this group is not within a statistically tight band of agreement. That lack of consensus underlines how much of the valuation work still comes back to an investor’s own conviction on long term crypto adoption and how Coinbase Global monetises that through trading, custody, and subscription lines.

Result: Fair Value of $247.39 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the Coinbase Global narrative can break if crypto adoption stalls or if regulators restrict key revenue lines and compress fee based earnings power.

Find out about the key risks to this Coinbase Global narrative.

Another View: Coinbase Global Through Sales Multiples

There is a very different message coming from simple sales ratios. Coinbase Global trades on a P/S of 5.6x, which looks expensive against the US Capital Markets industry at 3.3x and also above its own fair ratio of 4.1x that the market could move toward over time.

Peers are even richer at 10.6x P/S, so the stock screens cheaper than that group, yet still carries valuation risk if revenue or sentiment weakens and the multiple drifts closer to the fair ratio.

See what the numbers say about this price — find out in our valuation breakdown.

Next Steps

Mixed messages on Coinbase Global so far. If the push into tokenization, the recent price slide, and the valuation split leave you undecided, move fast and pressure-test the thesis against both the upside and the downside using 1 key reward and 1 important warning sign.

data.title: Dynatrace (DT) Bindplane Lands Leader Spot In 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant
data.description:
• Dynatrace (NYSE:DT) reported that its Bindplane product was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Observability Pipelines.
  • Bindplane, acquired by Dynatrace in April 2026, features as a Leader in the first-ever Magic Quadrant for this category.
  • Gartner’s 2026 Critical Capabilities report ranks Bindplane highly across multiple observability pipeline use cases, according to Dynatrace.
  • The Bindplane Magic Quadrant Leader recognition is only one part of the broader Dynatrace story that investors need to weigh. Take a look at 1 warning sign we have identified for Dynatrace.

This spotlight on Bindplane shows Dynatrace is not the only business linked to the broader observability and AI infrastructure theme, and there is a wider set of stocks to explore through 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Dynatrace focuses on observability software that helps digital businesses understand and manage complex systems across regions including North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. As a result, Bindplane slots into an existing toolkit aimed at monitoring sprawling, data heavy infrastructure.

3 things going right for Dynatrace that this headline doesn't cover.

Why does Bindplane’s Gartner Leader status matter for Dynatrace?

This recognition tells customers that Bindplane is one of the stronger offerings in the young observability pipelines category. Since Bindplane is OpenTelemetry native and uses AI to clean and route telemetry before it hits downstream tools, it can strengthen Dynatrace’s pitch as a central data control layer rather than just another monitoring product.

Does this change the Dynatrace Narrative investors have been using?

The Narrative already leans on log management and Bindplane outperforming initial ARR expectations as proof that a unified platform can deepen usage. Gartner’s Leader badge reinforces that part of the story by validating Bindplane’s role in observability pipelines, although it does not remove execution risks around DPS renewals, Arize integration or margin pressure.

See how these catalysts shape Dynatrace's path to a $61.26 fair value.

What should you watch next to see if this Bindplane news really matters?

The key test is whether Bindplane shows up clearly in usage and contract metrics, especially log consumption, cross sell and ARR tied to observability pipelines over the next few reported quarters. Investors can focus on how management quantifies Bindplane driven wins and whether multi product deals grow as a share of total ARR in upcoming earnings updates.
